cls: Antibiotic - natural penicillin (beta-lactam), repository/depot intramuscular form
quick: Not applicable; deep IM injection only
Penicillins considered acceptable; preferred for syphilis in pregnancy
summary: Procaine penicillin G is a repository (depot) intramuscular formulation of penicillin G that releases drug slowly from the injection site, giving prolonged but lower plasma levels than aqueous penicillin G. It is a narrow-spectrum bactericidal beta-lactam used for susceptible infections such as certain pneumococcal, streptococcal, syphilis and anthrax indications. The procaine component can cause an immediate non-allergic reaction (Hoigne syndrome) if inadvertently given intravascularly.
indications: Moderately severe infections due to penicillin-G-susceptible microorganisms that respond to sustained low serum levels
Syphilis and other Treponema pallidum infections (as part of recommended regimens)
Anthrax (cutaneous, and as part of treatment/prophylaxis regimens)
Diphtheria (adjunct to antitoxin), erysipeloid, rat-bite fever and Vincent's infection (susceptible)

dosage.n: Continue per infection; reserve for susceptible organisms

dosage.d: Dose and duration per disease stage and current treatment guidelines
dosage.n: Benzathine penicillin is often preferred; follow guidelines

dosage.d: 600,000-1.2 million units IM daily as part of regimen

dosage.n: Avoid in neonates where labeling cautions

admin: Administer by DEEP intramuscular injection into a large muscle mass only
Aspirate before injection to avoid inadvertent intravascular (especially intra-arterial) injection
Do NOT give intravenously - intravascular injection can cause severe systemic reactions
Rotate injection sites; in adults the upper outer quadrant of the buttock or lateral thigh
Have epinephrine and resuscitation equipment available for anaphylaxis
moa: Penicillin G is a bactericidal beta-lactam that binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits the transpeptidation step of bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan synthesis, leading to cell lysis. The procaine salt forms an insoluble depot at the IM site that dissolves slowly, providing prolonged, lower-level release of active penicillin.

absolute: History of hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis) to any penicillin
Known hypersensitivity to procaine / procaine-type local anesthetics
relative: History of allergy, especially to cephalosporins (cross-reactivity)
Conditions requiring rapid high blood levels (use aqueous penicillin G instead)

preg: Penicillins are generally considered acceptable in pregnancy; penicillin G is the treatment of choice for syphilis in pregnant women. Use when indicated.
lact: Penicillin G is excreted in breast milk in small amounts and is considered compatible with breastfeeding; monitor the infant for diarrhea, candidiasis or rash.
renal: Penicillin G is renally cleared; in significant renal impairment, accumulation can occur and high doses may cause neurotoxicity (seizures). Use cautiously and reduce dose/frequency in severe impairment.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is generally required.

major: Probenecid - reduces renal excretion, raising and prolonging penicillin levels (sometimes used intentionally)
moderate: Tetracyclines and other bacteriostatic antibiotics - may antagonize bactericidal action
minor: May reduce efficacy of oral contraceptives (theoretical)
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction tests; can affect Coombs test and some protein assays

common: Injection-site pain, induration or sterile abscess
serious: Anaphylaxis and other immediate hypersensitivity reactions
Immediate non-allergic reaction to procaine (anxiety, confusion, hallucinations - Hoigne syndrome) with intravascular injection
Seizures with very high levels (renal impairment)
emergency: Acute systemic procaine reaction after intravascular injection

monitoring: Observe for immediate hypersensitivity after each injection
Renal function with prolonged or high-dose therapy
counsel: Tell your healthcare provider about any previous reaction to penicillin, cephalosporins or local anesthetics
The injection may be painful and cause a firm lump at the site
A flu-like reaction (fever, chills) within hours of treating syphilis (Herxheimer) is expected and self-limited
Seek emergency care for rash, swelling, wheeze or difficulty breathing
Complete the full course as prescribed
pk: Detectable serum levels within 1-4 hours of IM injection
Lower peak than aqueous penicillin G, at about 1-4 hours
Effective serum levels sustained 12-24 hours due to slow depot release
Prolonged - allows once-daily dosing for many indications
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; do not freeze; shake suspension well before use
pearls: Depot form gives lower, sustained levels - NOT for serious infections needing high rapid levels (use aqueous penicillin G IV)
Always aspirate and inject deep IM - inadvertent intravascular injection can cause an acute procaine reaction (Hoigne syndrome)
Benzathine penicillin G, not procaine, is the standard for latent syphilis; follow current guidelines
Cross-reactivity with cephalosporins exists - take a careful allergy history
High accumulation in renal failure can cause neurotoxicity/seizures
missed: For a scheduled injection that is missed, give it as soon as possible and adjust the next dose timing as advised; maintain the prescribed interval. Do not give two depot doses close together.
overdose: Overdose can cause neuromuscular hyperexcitability and seizures, particularly with renal impairment; intravascular procaine exposure causes acute CNS/cardiovascular reactions. Management is supportive with seizure control; penicillin G is removed by hemodialysis.
